El zapoteco de Tlacolulita y el transyautepequeño, el legado lingüístico de Cosijoeza I (title on slides: 'El zapoteco de Tlacolulita y el grupo transyautepequeño del zapoteco central'). catalog_locator: Beam de Azcona 2023 JHL preprint, §2.1 p. 5 and §4.1.1 p. 17 with fn. 15; compound prominence: 2018 slides 33 and 38
catalog_quote: Since PTZ times, the root-initial syllable has been the most prominent in the phonological word. This syllable is stressed by Hyman’s (2006: 231) definition. I will refer to stressed syllables as “tonic syllables” … (14) Petapa Zapotec (a) PFV-crack … [bi˧ˈɾjaʰ˨sa˨] … Tone is most salient on the tonic syllable in this language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Beam de Azcona, Rosemary G. 2023. The tonal morphology of the potential in Coatec Zapotec (Di'zhke'): implications for early Zapotecan tone, *ʔ, and verb classes through internal and comparative reconstruction. Journal of Historical Linguistics 14(2): 179-241. Amsterdam: John Benjamins.
tone_statements.quote: In (14), the verb root ‘crack’, which is normally realized with low level tone, such as in the perfective form in (a), is pronounced with slightly higher pitch when it follows the high tone of the pre-tonic syllable in (b). Since this language does not have a contrastive mid tone, we can consider the pronunciation of the tonic syllable in (b) to be a higher-than-normal realization of the low tone. [...] among Petapa disyllables checked vowels /Vʔ/ are always low, whereas rearticulated vowels /VˀV/ are always high, though these phonation categories contrast on monosyllables with high tone (Beam de Azcona 2018).
tone_statements.locator: preprint p. 17, §4.1.1 'Upstep: The vestiges of pre-tonic tone' (ex. 14 'Petapa Zapotec'); and preprint p. 46, §5 'Conclusions'
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 level (L, H; no contrastive mid) per the Petapa passages

tone_statements.quote: Análisis suprasegmental y prosódico de Petapa [tabla; columnas: Tipo de fonación | Tonos | C2; se cita la columna Tonos] Modal | Bajo ˨ ~ ˧˩, “Alto” ˧ ~ ˩˧ Contornos antes de lenis, Niveles antes de fortis [...] Aspirada | Bajo, Alto Hay dos supuestos ejemplos de ascendente [...] Cortada | Bajo, Alto y Ascendente contrastan en monosílabos, la vocal es más larga en ascendente que en los otros dos En bisílabos siempre es bajo [...] Rearticulada | Siempre alto [...] Rearticulada aspirada | Siempre alto
tone_statements.translation: Suprasegmental and prosodic analysis of Petapa [table; columns: phonation type | tones | C2; the Tones column is quoted]. Modal: Low ˨ ~ ˧˩, 'High' ˧ ~ ˩˧; contours before lenis, levels before fortis. Breathy (aspirada): Low, High; there are two supposed examples of rising. Checked (cortada): Low, High and Rising contrast in monosyllables, the vowel is longer with rising than with the other two; in disyllables it is always low. Rearticulated: always high. Breathy rearticulated: always high.
tone_statements.locator: slide 12, 'Análisis suprasegmental y prosódico de Petapa'
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 (bajo, alto) + ascendente only on checked monosyllables

Tesis de maestría en Antropología Social, CIESAS Sureste. 206 pp. (repositorio CIESAS handle 1015/1555, open access CC BY-NC-SA)
sources.note: First-approximation phonology of 'zapoteco domingano' (Santo Domingo Petapa), pp. 137-139: six vowels (a e i o u æ), level and contour tones (alto, bajo, ascendente, descendente), three glottalized vowel types citing Benn 2021, consonant table. Only stress remark is anecdotal (p. 139 + fn. 163): one word [nà.ʃì.ˈjé] naxiyé 'oloroso' where speakers asked whether the last syllable 'llevaba acento' and chose to mark accent rather than tone; footnote asks whether stress is replacing tone in heritage speakers. sources.note: Petapa Zapotec: pre-tonic prefixes are toneless (mid pitch) except potential forms, where a floating H docks on the prefix and the following Low root is upstepped ([bi˧ˈɾjaʰ˨sa˨] PFV vs [gi˦ˈɾjaʰ˧sa] POT 'crack'); the language has no contrastive mid tone; High is realized extra-high; post-tonic syllables bear no contrastive tone of their own (tonal reduction, e.g. 'thorn' simplified to Low /gæ̀ʰt͡sæ/); among disyllables checked vowels are always Low and rearticulated vowels always High, contrasting only on High-toned monosyllables (citing Beam de Azcona 2018).

sources.note: The only modern phonological description that includes first-hand Petapa Zapotec data (Peña Godínez 2022 fn. 161: Benn did fieldwork in Santo Domingo Petapa and calls the variety 'zapoteco de Petapa'); a phonetics/phonology dissertation on the sister language Guienagati with comparative NETZ chapters is the most likely place for an explicit stress statement covering Petapa. Glottolog ref 671933 (phonology;comparative).
